capitals.name: Vengi (Pedavegi)
capitals.note: The page: "Their capital was located at Vengi, modern Pedavegi near Eluru in West Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh"; the coordinates are approximate (the page gives none). Until 324 the point lies inside the land andhra-ikshvaku draws (the page says the two rules "possibly overlapped"), so it is outside the drawn shape for those 25 years.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Salankayana row. The first version (Vijayawada 100 km + Rajahmundry 80 km, 160 cells) crossed the Krishna into the Guntur country, against the page's "Their territory was located between the Godavari and the Krishna rivers": 86 of its cells were the core of ananda-gotrika-dynasty_335 and 105 were andhra-ikshvaku_227 cells. Now the doab north of the Krishna (a 12-point polygon, 49 cells, about 12,300 km2) without the cells that andhra-ikshvaku draws until 325 (11 cells on the Godavari side). The page says the Ikshvaku "last extant inscription is from c. 325 CE" and calls the Salankayanas (c. 300-450) their successors "whose rule possibly overlapped with them", so the Ikshvaku claim is respected until 325. The capital Vengi (Pedavegi) lies in the excluded part until 325. Cliopatria leaves this land stateless after the Satavahana row ends (223).

ledger.note: 300: the Salankayanas rule Vengi. "ruled a part of Andhra region in India from 300 to 440 CE" and "Their territory was located between the Godavari and the Krishna rivers" (page, re-read for this repair); the earliest four inscriptions date to c. 300-350/400 CE. Drawn in the doab north of the Krishna without the land andhra-ikshvaku draws until 325 (the page: Ikshvaku "last extant inscription is from c. 325 CE", the Salankayanas their successors "whose rule possibly overlapped with them"). The page names no predecessor.

ledger.note: c. 325 (bridge): the Salankayanas hold the whole doab once the Ikshvaku inscriptions stop. "Ikshvaku dynasty, whose last extant inscription is from c. 325 CE, ruled the Krishna-Godavari region in the early 4th century. Their successors, whose rule possibly overlapped with them, included the Salankayanas (c. 300-450)" (page). The page does not say conquest or give a year for the transfer; 325 is the last Ikshvaku inscription. Mismatch to settle with the owner of andhra-ikshvaku: its /ledger/1 gives the whole 325 loss to late-pallava-empire (its page: the Pallavas conquered the dynasty), and late-pallava-empire has no matching gain; the Vijayawada part of that shape is the part drawn here.

ledger.note: 440: the Salankayana rule ends. The page gives 440 as the end and "c. 300-450" elsewhere, with the Vishnukundins (c. 422-612 on this page) displacing them "around the mid-5th century"; the Vishnukundina page puts Madhava Varma II's conquest of Vengi in his c. 440-460 reign. The page describes no conquest at 440.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks (named only through the vishnukundina-dynasty counterpart). Two pages opened (budget 2-5): Salankayana and Vishnukundina dynasty (for the successor). The page is thin: no reign years, only Hastivarman named (Penugonda inscription; Samudragupta "captured and released several kings of Dakshinapatha, including Hasti-varman of Vengi", undated, so he may have become a tributary: the Gupta dossier does not draw it). The dates conflict: 300-440 (text), c. 300-450 (table), displaced mid-5th century, conquered in the late 5th century (citation needed). The relation to the Pallavas (shared Skandavarman and Nandivarman names, bull seal) is reported as speculation only. Gazetteer names needed: Vengi (region), Pedavegi. REPAIR (2026-10-19, after review): the radius shape crossed the Krishna and double-drew 86 Ananda Gotrika cells and 105 Ikshvaku cells; now the doab north of the Krishna as a 12-point polygon (49 cells, about 12,300 km2 against 40,320 before), without the Ikshvaku cells until 325 (found 300 on 11 cells, gain 325 of the other 38 at confidence 1). Disagreement with the reviewer's example fix of subtracting the Guntur 100 km disc: that disc (ananda-gotrika-dynasty /keyframe_review/0) reaches Eluru, 86 km from Guntur, so subtracting it would remove the capital Vengi (Pedavegi near Eluru, Salankayana page) from the Salankayana shape; the 28 cells that remain in common with ananda-gotrika-dynasty_335 should be taken out of the Ananda Gotrika shape (restrict it to the south of the Krishna). The Salankayana page itself says the Salankayanas' rule "possibly overlapped" the Ikshvakus' and the Ananda-gotra kings' (c. 300-400). Thin gap: the Samudragupta page (opened) says Samudragupta "captured and released several kings of Dakshinapatha, including Hasti-varman of Vengi" and gives no year for the campaign (reign c. 335-375); the Salankayana page says only that the king "may have become a tributary", so no vassal event is drawn.
